AgentResult.description: What every runtime produces, regardless of which one ran the case.
AgentResult.title: AgentResult

Claim.description: A statement in the answer and the evidence refs it rests on.
Claim.title: Claim

ClaimVerification.description:
The verdict on one claim, with the rows it came from and the numbers
compared (ADR 0034). `claimed_value` and `recomputed_value` share a unit:
percentage points for growth and ratios, the row's unit for a level.
`tolerance` is the largest difference still counted as a match.
ClaimVerification.title: ClaimVerification

Company.description: A company the tools have data for.
Company.title: Company

DataSource.description: Where the tools' data comes from: SEC EDGAR or synthetic fixtures.
DataSource.title: DataSource

EvalRun.description: A full evaluation run, written to evals/results/<run_id>.json.
EvalRun.title: EvalRun

EvalSummary.description: One row of `GET /evals`: an eval run from `evals/results/`.
EvalSummary.title: EvalSummary

Evidence.description:
One tool row an answer cites, resolved by the server (ADR 0030).

The model cites a row by its `ref`. `verified` is true only when that ref
matches a row a tool returned in the same run; the source details and
`excerpt` then come from that row, never from the model. An unverified
ref keeps only `ref`, with `source_type="unknown"`.
Evidence.title: Evidence

Feedback.description:
Body of `POST /runs/{run_id}/feedback`: a human label on an answer,
the start of the judge-calibration set (#115).
Feedback.title: Feedback

InvestigateRequest.description:
Body of `POST /investigate`.

`mode`/`runtime` are left as plain strings, not a `Literal`, so an
unsupported value reaches the endpoint's own check and comes back as a 422
naming what's unsupported, rather than FastAPI's schema-level 400.
InvestigateRequest.title: InvestigateRequest

MetricRow.description:
One metric of both runs. `verdict` is "same", "better" or "worse" for a
gated metric of comparable runs, and None otherwise.
MetricRow.title: MetricRow

ResearchRun.description: One finished `POST /investigate`, as the run store keeps it.
ResearchRun.title: ResearchRun

RetrievalQuality.title: RetrievalQuality

RuntimeCapability.description: A runtime and whether this deployment can run it.
RuntimeCapability.title: RuntimeCapability

StoredFeedback.description: Feedback as stored with its run.
StoredFeedback.title: StoredFeedback

ToolCall.description: One tool invocation, in the order it was made.
ToolCall.title: ToolCall

TrajectoryScore.description:
The run path of one case, scored step by step from its recorded trace
without a model call (#116). None means not applicable or not measurable
for this case.
TrajectoryScore.title: TrajectoryScore

VerificationReport.description:
Every claim of one answer checked, and what that adds up to (ADR 0035).

The scores are None when nothing could be measured. `overall_verdict` is
the worst claim's verdict, UNVERIFIABLE for an answer with no claims.
VerificationReport.title: VerificationReport

VerifyRequest.description:
Body of `POST /verify`: an answer's claims and the tool rows they rest
on. A claim that cites refs is checked against those rows only; one that
cites none, against every row. Rows are `get_financial_fact` output.
VerifyRequest.title: VerifyRequest

get.description: What this deployment can run, so a client offers only that.
Every company the tools know, by ticker.

`candidate` judged against `baseline` by the gate. Runs it refuses come
back with `comparable: false` and the reasons, not as an error.
One eval run with its per-case scores.

Liveness only. Never checks a dependency — a probe that fails on a
database blip restarts a healthy pod.

One saved run: the question, settings, answer, claims, evidence and
tool calls.
A saved run as a JSON file to download.

post.description: A 👍/👎 and an optional note on a saved run, replacing any earlier one.

A verdict for each claim, and what they add up to. Claims the numeric
verifier can't read come back UNVERIFIABLE; an answer with no claims is
UNVERIFIABLE as a whole.
